text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 infection in newborns is generally rare and often mild, especially if the mother was vaccinated during pregnancy. Vaccination of pregnant women and children 6 months and older can help protect newborns and young children from severe outcomes of COVID-19, according to the CDC. While newborns can be infected with COVID-19, the risk of severe illness is low, particularly if the mother was vaccinated.

text_blocks.snippet: Key points about COVID-19 in newborns:

list.title: Low risk of severe illness:
list.snippet: If a mother is vaccinated during pregnancy, the risk of severe illness from COVID-19 in newborns is very low.

list.title: Vaccination is key:
list.snippet: Vaccinating pregnant women and children over 6 months old can help protect newborns from severe outcomes.

list.title: Observe for symptoms:
list.snippet: Parents should be aware of potential symptoms of COVID-19 in newborns, including breathing difficulties, which require immediate medical attention.

list.title: Breathing trouble:
list.snippet: Seek emergency help if a newborn has trouble breathing, such as grunting, flaring nostrils, or chest pulling with each breath.
